tradeoffs.android: In a folder, every file goes through Android’s storage provider, which is slower than the app’s own storage: books and covers open a little more slowly, and importing, converting and moving books takes noticeably longer. In return, file managers, other apps and a computer plugged in by USB can see the books, and they stay if nexlibris is uninstalled, which deletes its own storage. No permission is needed beyond the folder you pick.
tradeoffs.ios: In a folder, the books are files you can see in the Files app, and other apps, a computer (through iCloud Drive or a drive) and backups can reach them; they stay if nexlibris is deleted, which deletes its own storage. A folder in iCloud Drive is slower, as books not yet on the phone are downloaded when they’re opened. No permission is needed beyond the folder you pick.
tradeoffs.browser: In a folder, saving is slower: the browser writes each file to a temporary copy and checks it before putting it in place, so importing, converting and moving books takes longer than in its own storage, though reading is about as quick. The browser also asks again to let nexlibris use the folder after it restarts (one click; Chrome remembers if you choose “Allow on every visit”). In return, other apps and backups can see the books, and clearing the browser’s data for this site doesn’t delete them.

Then sync here again to take what the computer sent. Books’ files are only kept in the folder until the other side has them.

connections.deactivateTitle: Takes {name} out of the Library and Send to… on this device.
connections.activateTitle: Puts {name} in the Library and Send to… on this device, while it’s around.
connections.title: Connections
connections.empty: Add a reader or a folder to send books to, an OPDS catalog to publish them, an OPDS server to browse, or nexlibris on another device to share books with. Each one you send to has a catalog of books: add to it with “Add to…” on books, or give it a search whose matches are added.
connections.hostedLink: syncs with this device, last synced {when}
connections.offeredTitle: The books {name} offered this device when it last synced.
connections.fromTitle: Brings every book {name} shows this device that it doesn’t have.
connections.toTitle: Sends every book in its catalog that {name} doesn’t have. Nothing is deleted either side.
connections.forgetTitle: Unpairs {name}: it can’t sync with this device until it pairs again. The connection stays.
connections.readTitle: Brings in every book there that the library doesn’t have.
connections.writeTitle: Sends every book in its catalog that isn’t there yet, and newer copies of ones that changed. Nothing there is deleted.
connections.name: Name
connections.browseHelp: Browse its books in the Library and under “On it…”, and add them to the library from there. Nothing is sent to it.
connections.instanceSearchHelp: {name} sees the books matching this search, and books you add to it: their details, covers and files. It doesn’t see the others, and nothing either side deletes is deleted on the other.
connections.searchHelp: Books matching it, as in the search box (say, tag:xteink, or rating:4+ author:herbert), are added to its catalog beside the books you add to it, and stay there; take one out by hand to keep it out.
connections.folderHelp: Where its books are, on this computer (a backup drive, a reader that mounts as one). Each computer chooses it for itself; a manifest there, .nexlibris-library.json, keeps the books’ details.
connections.signInHelp: For a catalog that asks for one (HTTP Basic). Kept on this device only, sent only to the catalog’s own server.
connections.insecure: This address isn’t https, so the password would be sent unencrypted.

tookOut.one: Took {count} book deleted there out of its catalog.
tookOut.other: Took {count} books deleted there out of its catalog.

connections.catalogAdded: Added the catalog to the reader’s OPDS libraries.
connections.allThere: Everything in its catalog is already there.
connections.willAddCatalog: Will add the catalog at {url} to the reader’s OPDS libraries.
connections.deletedThere: Deleted there since the last sync, so taken out of its catalog rather than sent again: {titles}.

leftThere.one: {count} file no longer in its catalog left there as it is.
leftThere.other: {count} files no longer in its catalog left there as they are.

connections.keepFound: Keep copies of these books already on the device (put there by hand or by other software) rather than sending nexlibris’s. They’re sent again once the book’s file in the library changes.
connections.unsendable: Not sent, with no file the device reads: {titles}.
connections.notAllowed: nexlibris wasn’t allowed to write to {name}.
connections.staticCatalog: A static OPDS catalog of {books}, for hosting anywhere that serves files (it’s meant for the root of a site){at}. Books go as their files are; book files written before stay, even once out of the catalog.
connections.writtenTo: It’s written to the folder “{name}” on this computer; only what changed is copied.
connections.chooseToWrite: Choose a folder to write it to (the one your site is deployed from, say): later syncs update it in place.
connections.zipOnly: This browser can’t write to folders, so each sync saves the whole catalog as a zip.

alreadyUpToDate.one: ; {count} file was already up to date
alreadyUpToDate.other: ; {count} files were already up to date

connections.leftOut: {title}: left out, with no file in a format the catalog takes

status.update: the next sync sends a newer copy
status.left: no longer in its catalog: left there
status.changed: changed on the device, so left alone

connections.noCatalogYet: Nothing yet: the catalog hasn’t been written. Sync it to write it.

pending.one: {count} book in its catalog not on it yet: the next sync adds it.
pending.other: {count} books in its catalog not on it yet: the next sync adds them.

connections.importHelp: Importing copies a book into the library and keeps it on this connection.
connections.linkHelp: Put there some other way. Linking keeps them on this connection and lets syncs update them. One whose library copy has no file the connection takes can be imported instead, adding the device’s file to it.
connections.removeHelp: Removing one deletes it there and takes it out of the catalog, so syncs don’t send it again.

about.title: About nexlibris
about.tagline: A library for your books, wherever you read them.
about.intro: nexlibris keeps your ebooks, comics and documents in one library: it reads their details and covers, converts between formats, and sends books to your readers. It works in the browser, as a desktop app and on your phone, keeping the library on your own devices (or your own server), and syncs between them.
about.welcome: Welcome. Your library is empty: add some books to start, by importing files, a folder or a whole Calibre library, or by looking one up by its ISBN. You can also connect to nexlibris on another device and sync its library here.

import.title: Import
import.text: EPUB, Kindle books, PDF, comics, text and RTF, single files, folders or whole Calibre libraries, with their details and covers.

read.title: Read
read.text: Every format it imports opens in the reader, which keeps your place on every device.

convert.title: Convert
convert.text: Between formats, in the app itself: EPUB to Kindle books, PDF or RTF, comics between CBZ and CBR, and more.

send.title: Send to readers
send.text: CrossPoint readers, folders and drives, and OPDS catalogs, each with the books you choose for it.

sync.title: Sync
sync.text: Between your computer, phone and browser, over the network, Bluetooth or a shared folder, or through your own server.

search.title: Search
search.text: By any detail, with a search syntax like Gmail’s, and inside the books’ text.

about.appsIntro: The library is the same everywhere; the apps add what a browser can’t do, such as keeping it in a folder of your own.
